BiblicalUsage: Tachtim-chodshi was a place in the north, where Joab and the captains came on their journey to number Israel. The name means the lower part of a new moon, or the land of Tahtim-hodshi, and the place is named once, as a point on the census road. Its exact site is not known.
TheologicalSignificance: The census road matters, I believe, because it shows the cost of counting: Joab walked the whole land, and this far northern place is where the journey turned home.
